title: The month of Chet
hook: in Chet, remember the Lord and great joy comes (Barah Maha, ang 133)

segments.voice: Yesterday, veechhurhe: separated by our own deeds, and asking in mercy to be united. Today the year begins, with the first month and its spring.

The cold has finally gone. Mustard fields that were yellow all winter are going to seed. Wheat is turning gold and heavy, a few weeks from harvest. Trees push out new leaves overnight, and the koel, a bird with a rising call, starts singing in the mornings. This is Chet, roughly March into April in Punjab, when everything seems to come back. And Guru Arjan begins his year of longing here, in the season when you'd think nobody has any reason to long for anything.
screen: `THE COLD GONE, WHEAT GOING GOLD.` → `CHET: MARCH INTO APRIL IN PUNJAB.` → `LONGING IN THE SEASON OF PLENTY.`

segments.voice: Chet is the first month in Guru Arjan's Barah Maha, and the Nanakshahi calendar begins its year with Chet too. The stanza on ang 133 opens, in paraphrase: in Chet, by worshiping the Lord of the universe, a deep and lasting joy arises. Then it says how. Meeting the holy ones, the One is found, and the tongue repeats the Name. Those who have found their Lord, their coming into the world is counted. To live even a moment without the One is to waste a life. The One is present in water, on land, in the sky and in the forests, and those who don't keep the One in mind suffer much pain. It closes with a wish: I touch the feet of whoever brings me to meet that Lord in Chet. Notice the joy. It isn't the joy of the season, the sunshine and new leaves. It's the joy of remembering. Spring is everywhere, in water, land, sky and forest, because the One is everywhere in it, so the green outside becomes a reminder of what's inside it. Some Punjabi listeners also hear a play of sounds. Chet is the month, but chet is also an everyday word for awareness, for keeping something in mind, as in chete, remembering. The stanza never says it's a pun, so it's only a sound worth noticing. In the season when the world wakes up, the soul is asked to wake up too.
screen: `CHET: THE FIRST MONTH.` · `JOY FROM REMEMBERING THE ONE.` · `WATER, LAND, SKY AND FOREST.` · `CHET, AND CHET: REMEMBERING.` · then, large: `CHET: JOY.`

segments.voice: Picture a seed, what you'd plant, where, how deep; a pot will do, or even a kitchen scrap like a green onion root in water. As you picture it, breathe slowly and think of one thing in you that's been waiting to grow, and let the seed hold that wish. If you pray, you can say Waheguru over it.
Chet. Spring, the first month of Guru Arjan's Barah Maha: remembering the One brings deep joy, and the One fills water, land, sky and forest.
Your line: chet: joy. It comes from remembering, not from the weather. Day five hundred sixty-six: spring has started.

howItsDone: On the sangrand of Chet, gurdwaras that keep the day read the Chet stanza of Guru Arjan's Barah Maha, and in the Nanakshahi calendar Chet is the first month of the year.

chat.says: Spring's already a happy season. What joy does Guru Arjan find in the month of Chet?
options: Not the weather's joy: the deep joy of remembering the One, who fills water, land, sky and forest.
The joy of the new harvest, since a full granary is what the stanza calls lasting happiness.
The joy of a fresh start, since Chet wipes away every deed done in the year before it.
chat.meaning: The Chet stanza says lasting joy comes from worshiping and remembering the One, who is present in water, land, sky and forest.
